input: Brainstorm a name for my new bakery

candidate.taskDescription: Generate a creative and memorable name for your new bakery.

questions.title: What specific themes or concepts would you like the bakery to embody?
questions.description: Consider the type of bakery you are opening (e.g., artisanal bread, vegan, gluten-free) and any unique aspects you want to highlight.

questions.title: Have you already brainstormed any potential names or keywords?
questions.description: Share any ideas or words that come to mind, even if they are not fully formed.

questions.title: What is the target demographic for your bakery?
questions.description: Consider the age, lifestyle, and preferences of your potential customers.

questions.title: Do you have any specific words or phrases that are important to you or your brand?
questions.description: Share any meaningful words or phrases that you would like to incorporate into the name.

questions.title: What is the overall tone or personality you want the bakery to convey?
questions.description: Consider whether you want the name to be playful, sophisticated, rustic, etc.

questions.title: Have you considered the availability of the chosen name?
questions.description: Check if the name is already in use by another business or individual.

questions.title: What is your preferred format for the bakery name (e.g., short, long, descriptive)?
questions.description: Share your preference for the length and style of the name.

verdict.notes: Set B has notable redundancy (Q1 and Q4 both ask about themes/keywords; Q5 overlaps heavily with Q1), misses key practical unknowns (specialty baked goods, location, personal story), and Q6 ("Have you considered name availability?") is more of a reminder than a useful clarifying question. Set A is more concrete, broader in coverage, and avoids overlap better.

input: Throw a dinner party for 8 friends

candidate.taskTitle: Plan a Dinner Party for 8 Friends
candidate.taskDescription: Organize a dinner party for 8 friends, including food, seating, music, and coordination.

questions.title: What type of cuisine would you like to serve?
questions.description: Would you prefer a specific cuisine or a mix of different options?

questions.title: Do you have a preferred seating arrangement in mind?
questions.description: Would you like to sit in a specific area or mix it up for variety?

questions.title: What type of music would you like to play?
questions.description: Would you prefer upbeat, relaxing, or a mix of both?

questions.title: Have you already planned the menu for the dinner?
questions.description: Would you like help deciding on the dishes or prefer to do it yourself?

questions.title: Do you have any dietary restrictions or preferences for your guests?
questions.description: Would you like to accommodate any specific dietary needs?

questions.title: Would you like to hire a DJ or just play music from a playlist?
questions.description: Would you prefer live music or pre-recorded tracks?

questions.title: Have you already coordinated with your friends to arrive at the same time?
questions.description: Would you like help with timing or logistics?

verdict.notes: Set B wastes questions on minor logistical details (seating arrangement, music type, DJ vs. playlist, arrival coordination) while missing critical unknowns like date, venue, budget, and whether the host is cooking or catering. Questions 1 and 4 are also redundant — asking about cuisine type and then whether the menu is already planned heavily overlap — and questions 3 and 6 repeat the same music theme.

candidate.taskDescription: Determine a suitable therapist for your needs.

questions.title: What specific area of concern would you like to address with therapy?
Do you prefer in-person or online therapy sessions?
What is your budget for therapy sessions?
How many therapy sessions are you willing to commit to initially?
Have you owned a therapist before, and if so, what was your experience?
What is your current living situation like?
Are there any specific therapists or practices you are interested in?

verdict.notes: Set B contains a glaring error ("Have you owned a therapist before") that makes it nonsensical and unprofessional, and it omits critical planning variables like location and urgency. Questions about "number of sessions to commit to" and "current living situation" are either premature or irrelevant for finding a therapist, making the set poorly targeted and less useful than Set A.

questions.description: Please specify the reason for your appointment.

questions.description: Please provide any relevant information.

verdict.notes: Set B splits date and time into two separate questions (wasting two slots on a single logistical concern) and then fills the remaining slots with clinical intake questions (dietary restrictions, current medications) that are irrelevant to the task of *booking* an appointment. It also omits critical planning unknowns: who the appointment is for, urgency, preferred booking method, and in-person vs. remote preference — all of which Set A covers efficiently.

input: Update my resume for a product manager role

candidate.taskTitle: Update my resume for a product manager role

verdict.notes: Set B wastes two of its seven slots on irrelevant or low-value questions (salary range and portfolio/evidence) that don't help plan a resume update, and it misses critical unknowns like the applicant's current job title, seniority/level of PM role, and whether there's a specific job posting to target. The phrasing of Q1 also oddly uses first-person "I" instead of second-person "you," which feels robotic and misaligned.

input: Untangle my German tax returns for 2020-2024

candidate.taskDescription: Sort and file German tax documents for the years 2020-2024.

questions.title: Have you already printed and filed the 2020-2024 German tax returns?
questions.description: Please confirm if you have completed this step.

questions.title: Do you have any folders or digital organization systems for storing these tax documents?
questions.description: Describe your current filing method.

questions.title: Are there any discrepancies or errors in the 2020-2024 tax returns that need attention?
questions.description: List any issues you have encountered.

questions.title: Have you reviewed and verified the accuracy of the income and deductions for each year?
questions.description: Explain your verification process.

questions.title: Do you have access to the necessary German tax filing software or tools?
questions.description: Describe the software or tools you are using.

questions.title: Have you consulted with a tax professional or accountant for assistance with any complex tax issues?
questions.description: Provide details of any professional help you have sought.

questions.title: Do you need to obtain any additional permits or approvals for filing these tax returns?
questions.description: List any permits or approvals required.

verdict.notes: Set B asks largely yes/no, surface-level questions (e.g., "do you have folders?", "permits or approvals?") that don't uncover the key unknowns needed to plan German tax untangling — namely employment status, residency, outstanding filings, urgency, or which Finanzamt is involved. Questions 3 and 4 overlap heavily (both about accuracy/errors), and question 7 about "permits or approvals" is nonsensical for personal tax returns, severely hurting specificity and coverage.

input: Plan our wedding for next summer

candidate.taskDescription: Plan the details of our wedding for next summer.

questions.title: What is the preferred date for our wedding that works for you and your guests?
What is your budget for the wedding?
Do you have access to a venue that suits our budget and preferences?
Do you have access to photographers who can capture the day of the wedding?
Do you have the necessary permits and licenses to hold a wedding in our chosen location?
Do you have access to a catering service that can provide a variety of food options?
Do you have the necessary equipment and supplies to set up the wedding venue and decorations?

verdict.notes: Set B's questions are oddly framed as "do you have access to X" checklists rather than open discovery questions, missing critical unknowns like guest count, location, and wedding style/theme entirely. Several questions also awkwardly embed multiple assumptions (e.g., Q3 bundles budget and preferences; Q5 assumes a "chosen location" not yet established), making them feel robotic and premature rather than genuinely exploratory.
